message.content:
VERDICT: schedule
WHY: No security fixes and no breaking config or API changes across the 12 releases - it's mostly new model support (Muse Glimmer, Nemotron, Qwen 3.8) plus dependency updates. However, v0.32.15 and v0.33.0 fix real hangs (chat/generate wedging after parser errors, cancelled prefills) and roughly halve time-to-first-token via metadata caching, which are worth getting on a serving component. The minor boundary at v0.33.0 is feature-driven (Claude Desktop gateway support), not a migration.
WHAT_IT_WILL_TAKE: Nothing beyond the normal update process - no config format changes, migrations, or CLI behavior changes are mentioned in any of the release notes.
message.reasoning: No security fixes, no breaking changes. Mostly new model support, caching improvements, bug fixes. Verdict: defer. Though v0.33.0 fixes hangs and caching — meaningful but not urgent. Could argue schedule for the hang fixes and TTFT improvements. The notes fix "a bug where chat and generate could wedge" and "fixed a hang where agent clients cancel long prefills" — those are real fixes but not stated as actively broken for Matt. Routine-ish. I'd say defer, or schedule. The caching improvements (TTFT halved, hang fixes) are meaningful performance fixes worth doing deliberately. I'll go schedule.
